body.text: How do international patients request a specialist medical second opinion in Istanbul?

Major Istanbul tertiary hospitals run dedicated international patient departments that accept remote second-opinion requests before you book a flight, as well as structured in-person consultations when physical examination or repeat diagnostics are required. Submitting organized English summaries directly to the hospital's official portal lets department heads review your case before you travel.

Always verify that the hospital holds a Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate through the [Ministry of Health authorized facilities directory](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/TR-118173/uluslararasi-saglik-turizmi-yetki-belgesi-sahibi-araci-kuruluslar.html). Direct international desks at institutions such as [Koç University Hospital](https://www.kuh.ku.edu.tr/plan-your-visit/international-visitors) typically return preliminary written specialist reviews within three to five business days once complete imaging and lab reports arrive.
What DICOM imaging and medical records should be prepared safely?

Cardiologists and orthopedic surgeons cannot give a reliable second opinion from printed screenshots or low-resolution PDFs alone. You need original uncompressed [DICOM (Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine)](https://implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au/standards/organisation/digital-imaging-and-communications-in-medicine-dicom) files—the universal clinical standard documented in [NIH PMC medical imaging literature](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10610864/)—allowing Turkish radiologists and surgeons to scroll through every slice of your MRI, CT angiogram, or echocardiogram.

Upload sensitive clinical files strictly through the hospital's own encrypted patient portal or bring an encrypted USB drive directly to your consultation rather than sending records over unencrypted messaging apps. Prepare the following packet before your appointment:

items: Raw DICOM folders for recent cardiac MRI, coronary CT, echocardiogram clips, or orthopedic joint/spine MRI and X-rays
Chronological one-page medical history listing diagnoses, prior surgeries, and current medication doses
Official pathology, catheterization, or operative reports in English (or certified English translation)
Written list of three to five clinical questions you want the specialist to answer in writing

body.text: How does ITO coordinate multi-specialty hospital appointments and medical interpreters?

When a complex cardiology or orthopedic case requires opinions across two separate hospital groups—or coordination between an interventional cardiologist, orthopedic surgeon, and physiotherapist—scheduling overlaps quickly become stressful. [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about) is run by its two founders in Türkiye on a transparent flat client fee: paid by our clients, independent of provider commissions.

Through our [medical travel coordination service](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism), we align consultation calendars across your chosen hospitals, arrange private point-to-point Istanbul transfers to beat cross-Bosphorus traffic, and confirm hospital-provided or independent medical interpreters when needed. Because we never accept hospital kickbacks, you remain free to compare two hospitals objectively or return home with a conservative non-surgical plan.
Which JCI-accredited hospital groups serve international patients?

Istanbul hosts several large multidisciplinary tertiary hospitals that hold Joint Commission International (JCI) accreditation and maintain full-time international patient centers for cardiology, cardiovascular surgery, joint replacement, spine surgery, and sports orthopedics. Because JCI accredits individual hospital buildings rather than entire corporate brands, always verify the exact campus you plan to visit.

faq.q: How many days in Istanbul are needed for an in-person second opinion?
faq.a: Plan three to four days if you are consulting one or two specialists and may need repeat imaging such as a 3T joint MRI, stress echocardiogram, or CT angiogram before receiving a final written opinion.

faq.q: Are remote second opinions at Turkish hospitals free or paid?
faq.a: Some hospital international desks offer complimentary preliminary reviews to outline potential treatment pathways, while formal written multidisciplinary or pathology second opinions often carry a transparent consultation fee. Confirm terms upfront.

faq.q: Will I receive my Istanbul second opinion in English?
faq.a: Yes. JCI-accredited hospitals serving international patients issue English consultation notes, updated radiology reports, and digital DICOM copies of any new scans performed during your visit.

faq.q: Can I compare second opinions from two different Istanbul hospitals on one trip?
faq.a: Yes. Seeing two independent specialists across separate hospital groups is common for major cardiac or joint-replacement decisions. ITO schedules realistic transfer buffers between European-side and Asian-side campuses.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye review my medical scans or recommend surgery?
faq.a: No. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions. ITO handles independent travel, scheduling, and practical Istanbul logistics only.

faq.q: How do I contact ITO to coordinate a second-opinion visit in Istanbul?
faq.a: Message our two founders via [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism) with your preferred travel window and the specialties you plan to consult. For your privacy and security, please do not share passport or ID scans, medical records, or payment details in your first enquiry.
